Lina Gomez: Quick sync: thinking about a split-controlplane pattern where an edge auth proxy handles client TLS + auth in our region, and the customer-specific endpoint only handles model/data plane. Wanted tradeoffs captured.
Markus Reed: So proxy keeps client-facing certs and does authn/z, then mTLS to per-customer endpoint over peering?
Lina Gomez: Exactly. Idea is to minimize the number of private endpoints and avoid route table explosion while keeping per-customer data isolation behind the peering.
Tara O'Neill: Sounds reasonable. Primary risk is that proxy becomes a higher-trust surface (it sees plaintext client metadata). How do we preserve isolation guarantees?
Lina Gomez: We can enforce strict header-less pass-through of payloads and only forward a signed assertion token to the endpoint. No customer data stored at proxy.
Markus Reed: Another trade: cost and failure blast radius. Proxy centralization reduces ENI/PrivateLink counts but increases impact of an outage. Need autoscaling + regional redundancy.
Tara O'Neill: Also peering churn: if we fan many endpoints behind proxy, the peering/bgp table could spike when endpoints scale. AWS route limit per VGW/RT is a hard constraint.
Lina Gomez: True. One mitigation is to use a small set of regional transit endpoints and then use a per-customer routing key inside our overlay (L3 tunnel or GRE), so AWS route count stays small. That pushes complexity into our dataplane.
Markus Reed: What about TLS rotation semantics? If proxy handles TLS, endpoint cert rotation becomes invisible to clients, which is nice. But we still need to manage mTLS between proxy and endpoint and ensure zero-downtime rotation there.
Tara O'Neill: mTLS can use short-lived certs minted by central CP; design must account for connection pool reuse at proxy. Add a reconnection trigger when cert epoch increments.
Lina Gomez: Good point — add epoch-ping: proxy watches a signed epoch header and forces upstream connection drain on change.
Ops Bot: Deploy note: created canary group "proxy-split-alpha" with 10 customers -> rollout automation pending
Markus Reed: Also consider PrivateLink vs Peering: PrivateLink gives fewer route entries but per-VPC endpoint costs. Peering allows native routing but scales poorly for many tenants. Cost model needed.
Tara O'Neill: Also document failure modes: NAT timeouts for mobile clients hitting proxy, DNS caching issues if we ever flip client IPs, and how rollback to per-customer endpoint-only is performed.
Lina Gomez: Rollback plan: operator script toggles proxy->passthrough mode per-customer and concurrently batch-updates route mappings. Need staged batches and a kill-switch.
security-bot: Security note: require attestation for proxy instances and signed audit trails for any token minting. Also record any header injection operations.
Markus Reed: Perf note: measure end-to-end RTT addition of proxy, p99 tail for TLS handshake, and token verification latency. Keep budget under 10ms median extra.
Tara O'Neill: I'll write a short follow-up RFC with architecture diagram, protocol for signed assertion, epoch rotation, and rollback playbook. Include cost/scale appendix.
Lina Gomez: Thanks — will assign owners for the cost model and the staging chaos tests.
